input: nums is a nonempty plain dense Array of distinct Number integers obtained by rotating a strictly increasing array by any number of positions, including zero. Duplicates and empty input are outside the declared domain. Preconditions are not checked at runtime.
return: The minimum input value as a Number integer. A singleton returns its sole element. The minimum index remains in the closed interval [left, right] until the bounds meet; this differs explicitly from the half-open lower-bound search helpers.
mutation_aliasing: No input writes, sorting or copies. The result is an immutable numeric scalar. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Input values are safe integers in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]; NaN, infinities, BigInt and sparse arrays are excluded. With 1 <= n <= 4294967295, all indices and midpoint arithmetic are exact Numbers. The midpoint uses Math.floor without bitwise truncation. No arithmetic is performed on input values. Signed-zero identity is not distinguished.
complexity: n is the input length. O(log(n + 1)) time and O(1) auxiliary space under constant-cost indexing and machine-word comparisons. Each iteration strictly shrinks the closed candidate interval.
